nodes.label: S-ID.B.5

placement.meaning: High school band, not an exact year

nodes.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables. For example, collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?
nodes.label: 8.SP.A.4

nodes.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. nodes.label: 2.G.A.3

nodes.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b. *Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
nodes.label: 3.NF.A.1

nodes.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. edges.reason: Relative frequency is count divided by total and applies to any categorical tally. Grouped distribution tables are a common context but need not come first.
edges.scope: source of counts used to compute frequency

edges.reason: The criterion explicitly converts relative frequency to percentage.

Division introduces equal sharing, a useful conceptual bridge. Folding one whole into equal paper parts establishes a unit fraction without division notation or the inverse-multiplication interpretation.

Long division by one digit needs digit products during quotient trials, not the full multi-digit-by-one-digit column multiplication algorithm. That fuller algorithm can help verify a quotient but is optional.
edges.scope: checking quotients and the place-value multiplication pattern

edges.reason: For divisors seven, eight and nine, quotient-digit trials use the corresponding multiplication/division facts as numerical components.
edges.scope: partial quotients when the divisor is 7, 8 or 9
